summary.statement: Account managers or CSRs compare the issued policy line by line against the quote, application, proposal and AMS data, often by eye and with checklists.
Practice is inconsistent: some agencies let each account manager decide how thoroughly to check, and junior staff often do it.
Many agencies outsource checking (Patra, India-based BPOs) and account managers then handle the discrepancy reports.
A fast-growing share now uses AI checkers (Outmarket, Fulcrum, Vertafore Policy Check Agent, Epic Conductor) with human review of flagged items.
Vendor figures imply a manual check takes roughly 30–60 minutes per policy (Applied claims 32–60 minutes saved per check).
Outsourced checks have taken two weeks or more, followed by about an hour of manual AMS updates per policy at one brokerage.
Policies that don't come through carrier download are keyed in by hand; one agency says most of its farm policies don't download.
No public data gives weekly hours per account manager for checking or non-download entry.
Accounting staff reconcile carrier statements against AMS invoices by hand or in spreadsheets; mismatches are routed back to servicing staff.
Setup errors on the policy (wrong premium payable entity) block agency-bill reconciliation, matching the idea's 'configuration mismatch' claim.
Applied now ships AI agency-bill reconciliation in Applied Recon and Epic Conductor; Comulate and Ascend automate direct bill.
A paid budget line exists: agencies outsource policy checking to Patra and India-based BPOs, priced per policy or per FTE.
Reconciliation is a salaried role (e.g. $60k–$65k for a carrier payables specialist).
No public per-policy price for outsourced checking was found, so the $5–$10 per policy hypothesis is untested.
Agency owners decide whether staff adopt another tool.
For Epic integrations, Applied effectively holds a veto: it cut Comulate's Epic integration and the court declined to force it back.
No source names a specific approval role (CFO vs operations director) for AMS-adjacent tools.
Renewal-season backlogs and E&S volume are cited as reasons to adopt policy-review automation.
AI adoption is rising (46% of agencies) but formal deployment is low (14%), and E&O carriers advise a parallel-run period first.
One in seven agents files an E&O claim a year, about 20% coverage-related; manual checking is said to catch about 95% of errors.
Outsourced and AI checks both miss errors (a missed address change; an AI vendor that did not check tower defense coverage).
The leading E&O cause is failure to procure coverage, which issued-policy checking may not address.

new_unknowns.question: Since Applied (Epic Conductor) and Vertafore (Policy Check Agent) shipped native policy checking in Oct 2026, what share of mid-sized agencies will still buy a third-party checker, and for which lines (E&S, complex commercial)?
Can a sidecar integrate with Applied Epic through sanctioned channels (Applied certification/Ivans) without the platform risk shown in Applied v. Comulate?
